findings.evidence: Full thickness skin necrosis with sparing of skin islands (arrows) on left leg

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a real patient showing full-thickness skin necrosis on the left leg with arrows marking spared skin islands, matching the captioned manifestation of warfarin-induced skin necrosis in an article specifically titled for this disease.
panels.attribution_text: Nsaful et al. Warfarin-induced skin necrosis: a rare condition.. Ghana medical journal 2020. doi:10.4314/gmj.v54i4.10. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Full thickness skin necrosis with sparing of skin islands (arrows) on left leg
in_text_mentions: Skin necrosis on the left lower limb involved the entire leg up to the knee and foot sparing only part of the sole (Figure 3). The 4th toe eventually became gangrenous and was amputated. There was a large necrotic patch with eschar on the posterior aspect of the right lower limb.

findings.label: Full-thickness skin necrosis
findings.evidence: Figure 1 caption: "Warfarin-induced skin necrosis"; image shows a large central black necrotic eschar

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the patient's back showing a large, sharply demarcated necrotic eschar with an erythematous border, matching the captioned warfarin-induced skin necrosis and the in-text description of coalescing ecchymoses with tender erythematous lesions. Article title and caption specifically attribute the lesion to warfarin-induced skin necrosis. Patient was a 14-year-old female (adolescent) per article title.
panels.attribution_text: Zahra et al. Warfarin-Induced Skin Necrosis in a 14-Year-Old Female: A Case Report.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.30354. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: However, within three days of being discharged, the patient returned to the hospital's emergency department with painful back lesions. Examining her back revealed skin lesions with coalescing ecchymoses and incredibly tender erythematous lesions that were extremely painful to the touch (Figure 1).
panels.copyright: Zahra et al. Warfarin-Induced Skin Necrosis in a 14-Year-Old Female: A Case Report.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.30354. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.

findings.label: Full-thickness skin necrosis
findings.evidence: violaceous-to-black dusky patches with areas of necrosis overlying the left breast, pannus, right upper extremity, and left inner groin extending onto the left thigh

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of the abdomen/pannus showing a large ecchymotic-to-necrotic plaque. The caption explicitly attributes the ecchymoses to warfarin-induced skin necrosis, and the in-text description supports pannus/abdominal involvement with areas of necrosis. The article title identifies the case as atypical.
panels.attribution_text: Sklar and Messman. An Atypical Case of Warfarin-Induced Skin Necrosis.. Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine 2017. doi:10.5811/cpcem.2017.3.33373. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure Image 1.
panels.figure_caption: Ecchymoses secondary to warfarin-induced skin necrosis (arrow).
in_text_mentions: examination revealed sharply demarcated, mildly indurated and excruciatingly tender, violaceous-to-black dusky patches with areas of necrosis overlying the left breast, pannus, right upper extremity, and left inner groin extending onto the left thigh (Images 1, 2). Laboratory studies were significant for a normal platelet level of 180,000/mm,3 partial thromboplastin time of 27.7 sec, prothrombin time of 21.8 sec, and an international normalized ratio (INR) of 1.87. Computerized tomography (CT) of the abdomen with and without intravenous contrast showed no evidence of malignancy or hemorrhage.
panels.copyright: Sklar and Messman. An Atypical Case of Warfarin-Induced Skin Necrosis.. Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine 2017. doi:10.5811/cpcem.2017.3.33373. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure Image 1.

plate_findings.evidence: Erythema progression ... A: Left lower extremity day four
visual: dark violaceous/ecchymotic plaque-like area within the erythematous lesion

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of the left lower extremity showing a large erythematous/violaceous lesion with dark ecchymotic change and captioned progression to blood-filled bullae, consistent with warfarin-induced skin necrosis. Blue marker annotations are present. B: Clinical photograph of the right lower extremity showing a scattered macular erythematous rash in a patient with warfarin-induced skin necrosis; the finding is captioned as macular rash development, though it is less specific than the classic necrotic/bullous lesions. Blue marker annotation is present.
panels.attribution_text: Wali et al. Warfarin-Induced Skin Necrosis Despite Enoxaparin Bridging Therapy.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.20883. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Erythema progression and macular rash development. A: Left lower extremity day four. B: Right lower extremity day four.
in_text_mentions: Over the next day, the erythema increased in size and progressed to blood-filled bullae (Figure 2A). The patient also began developing minor macular rashes over the abdomen (not pictured) and the previously unaffected right lower extremity (Figure 2B). No lymphadenopathy was appreciated on physical examination.
panels.copyright: Wali et al. Warfarin-Induced Skin Necrosis Despite Enoxaparin Bridging Therapy.. Cureus 2022. doi:10.7759/cureus.20883. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
